rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ 'Electrons move at the speed of light in a wire.' ✅ Electrons move at a very slow *drift velocity* (mm/s); the *electric field* (the signal) travels near the speed of light.  ·  ❌ 'Electric current is the flow of electrons only.' ✅ By convention, current is defined as the *flow of positive charge*. In many cases (like electrolytes), negative charges also flow, but current is still in the opposite direction of electron flow.
